messages:
oliver: Quick check-in — ran a ~2h profile on canary serving with kernel-selection + kv-prefetch toggled. Dropping top-level notes and a link to the draft dashboard: https://dash.internal/rw/token-attrib-1901 :eyes:

oliver: TL;DR: TTFT regressions on long-context tails are mostly in 'kernel_queue' time, not decode compute. KV prefetch hit-rate looks correlated with the queue spikes.

sasha: Nice. Can you paste the top example trace? short snippet is fine.

oliver: Sure — here's one token trace (sanitized):
```
token_trace {
  token_idx: 124
  ttft_ms: 38.6
  decode_ms: 12.1
  kernel_queue_ms: 24.3
  kernel_exec_ms: 1.8
  kv_prefetch: false
  route: /v1/chat/gen
}
```

maria: That pattern (queue >> exec) suggests scheduling/backpressure. Are these requests hitting the hot-shard that does large KV merges?

oliver: Yup — same shard. When kv_prefetch=true we see: ttft_ms 12-16ms, kernel_queue_ms 6-8ms. So prefetch helps a lot on hot-prefixes.

dan: What's our sampling config? We shouldn't be paying much overhead for token traces.

oliver: Sampling is 1/200 requests, token-level traces only for requests > 256 tokens, and we only enable full kernel attribution in canary. Overhead measured ~0.4% p99 latency increase.

jen: For the dashboard, can we separate TTFT into: prequeue_ms (scheduling), kernel_queue_ms (handoff), kernel_exec_ms (compute), decode_ms (post-kernel prep)? Folks keep confusing prequeue vs kernel_queue.

metric-bot: New metric suggestion logged: metric.request_token_breakdown.{prequeue_ms,kernel_queue_ms,kernel_exec_ms,postproc_ms} (tags: model, route, shard, kv_prefetch)

maria: Also add kv_prefetch_hit boolean tag and kv_cache_size_kb tag — helps filter noisy samples from large-context pinned requests.

dan: Will adding those tags explode cardinality? We should cap bucketed kv_cache_size into low/med/high.

oliver: Agreed — propose kv_cache_bucket = {small, medium, large} + kv_prefetch_hit boolean. That keeps cardinality predictable.

sasha: For kernel attribution, are we confident kernel_exec_ms is purely compute? We saw a small plateau that looks like memcpy / device-sync.

oliver: Good call — current kernel_exec_ms includes device sync waits. I added a followup probe to split that into compute_ms and device_sync_ms in the next patch.

jen: Can we also add route-level SLOs on kernel_queue_ms p90/p99? Product wants per-route KPIs to trigger routing fallback (eg. route -> cheaper model)

oliver: Yes — the new dashboard draft includes per-route p50/p90/p99 for each bucket. Link again: https://dash.internal/rw/token-attrib-1901 — feedback welcome.

maria: One operational note — when we turned on aggressive prefetch in staging yesterday we saw less tail but higher average memory pressure on the CUDA nodes. Need to balance prefetch aggressiveness with eviction policies.

dan: Can we add an opt-in tracing flag per-customer for Dedicated so customers can sample traces without touching host-wide sampling?

oliver: That's in roadmap — private deployments + dedicated customers will get a tenant trace toggle. I'll file a tracking issue.

sasha: Action items?

oliver: 1) Split kernel_exec_ms -> compute_ms + device_sync_ms (oliver)
2) Add kv_cache_bucket + kv_prefetch_hit tags (maria/dan)
3) Dashboard: per-route kernel_queue SLOs + sampling controls (jen/sasha)
4) Add capped-cardinality guidelines to metrics docs (metric-bot)

jen: I'll take (3), add a canary alert rule for kernel_queue p99 > 20ms on high-throughput routes.

metric-bot: Issue created: INF-4128 "token-attrib: split kernel time + add kv tags" (assignee: oliver, maria).

oliver: Thanks all — plan to push the tracing split early next week to canary. Ping me if you want access to the raw trace dumps. :thumbsup:
